checks.name: FINDING 1 [partly retracted, see FINDING 3]: q ~2.2x rarer than Gaussian at SMALL n
checks.detail: For a centered bivariate normal with correlation rho, two iid draws give q_Gauss = 1/2 - arcsin(rho)/pi exactly. If measured q tracked it, the pairwise route would merely RESTATE rho > 0 and the 138x margin would be an illusion -- that was the outcome to rule out. Exact over n = 15..18: rho = ['0.91273961', '0.9146104', '0.91632008', '0.918422'], q measured = ['0.0631138', '0.0606892', '0.0605907', '0.0600657'], q Gaussian = ['0.133963', '0.132497', '0.131145', '0.129464'], ratio = ['0.47113', '0.45804', '0.46201', '0.46396'] -- settling near 0.4638, spread 0.0131. Discordance is ~2.2x rarer than a Gaussian with the SAME correlation. PARTLY RETRACTED: sampled at n = 50..800 the ratio RISES to 0.586, 0.688, 0.738, 0.768, 0.792 -- the non-Gaussian advantage is a SMALL-n effect and erodes toward 1, so the route is asymptotically tied to the same correlation after all. See the docstring's FINDING 3.

checks.name: FINDING 2: the target is Kendall's tau, with a ~15x margin on q alone
checks.detail: 1 - 2q is KENDALL'S TAU, so 'q < 1/2' is exactly tau > 0 -- a RANK statement, invariant under monotone reparametrisation, neither implied by nor implying Pearson rho > 0. At n = 18: tau = 0.879869 against the Gaussian-implied (2/pi) arcsin(rho) = 0.741072, so the rank dependence is STRONGER than the linear one. And M_1 > 0 needs less than tau > 0: it needs [q/(1-q)] * [mean ratio] < 1, and the mean ratio is separately ~0.111 (previous probe), so q < 0.90 suffices against a measured q = 0.0600657 -- a ~15x margin on q ALONE. Two sufficient routes: (q < 1/2 and mean ratio <= 1), or (q < 0.90 and mean ratio <= 0.111). NOT CLOSED -- both still need a statement about the joint law; what changed is that the target is a rank quantity with a margin, not a Pearson sign with none.
